label: input o at one of the first three positions
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is the letter o at sequence position 0, 1 or 2. Every such step is active (precision 1.0). Magnitude falls with position: o at t=0 reaches about the max (~1.0 relative), at t=1 about 0.5-0.6, at t=2 about 0.1-0.16. t=0 holds about 60% of the activation mass, t=1 32%, t=2 8%. It does not fire on o later in the original sequence (t>=3), on any other token, or on the delimiter. The rare misses (0.3% of mass) are weak echoes when o was the first token and comes back in as the input during copy step L+1 (or at t=4/5 in short sequences).

issues: No refuting evidence. Precision is 1.0 on test with 0 false positives, so the feature fires on every o at t<=2. Recall is 0.982 and mass recall 0.997.

Mass shares check out on the dev profile: t=0 0.596, t=1 0.317, t=2 0.083. Active counts per position are about equal (~16.7k each), so mean magnitude relative to t=0 is about 0.53 at t=1 and 0.14 at t=2. This is consistent with the claimed decay.
Firing is 100% on in_tok=o and zero on the delimiter. t=3 fires 3 times out of 500k; (o & t==3) scores F1 ~0.

All 897 test misses (0.3% of mass) belong to one class, as the explanation says: sequences that start with o, at copy step L+1 (recall_idx=1), where the o comes back in as input, at t=4/5 with L=3/4. Activations are 0.00-0.16. Adding this class to the predicate (o & recall_idx==1 & L<=4) lifts recall to ~1.0 but drops precision to 0.962 (F1 0.981, below the original 0.991), because most such echoes don't fire. So it is a documented, low-mass edge case, not a gap in the predicate.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
